title: IT'S YOUR MONEY
raw_text:
It’s Your Money
This page is available to provide you with a better understanding of how your state dollars are being spent.  All of the information contained on this page has been available to the public.
More information about state government is available on
Facebook
, and by signing up for Email Updates on my
homepage
.
Salary
As of December 1, 2025, my salary is $113,591.
Mileage and Expense Reimbursement
I do not use a state-owned or state-leased vehicle. Each month, I submit a statement of miles traveled on Senate business to the Senate’s Chief Clerk, requesting reimbursement. The current mileage reimbursement rate, established by the Internal Revenue Service, is 72.5 cents per mile. I use the per diem method of expense reimbursement for lodging and meals when I travel to Harrisburg for session.  Per diem rates are established by the United States General Services Administration.
District Offices
I have three district offices: one in Oil City, one in Warren, and one in Butler.  The monthly rent for each of these offices is $1358.40 (Oil City), $143.91 (Warren) and $1502.00 (Butler).
Additional Information
As a state legislator I have always supported efforts to make information about state government — particularly government spending — more easily accessible to the public.
Open Records Law
Pennsylvania’s Open Records Law (
Act 3 of 2008
), which I supported, makes many government records easily available to interested residents. Information about how to request records from any state executive branch office or local government office is available from the
Office of Open Records
. Information about requesting records from the
Senate
, the
House
, and the state
Judiciary
is also available.
Online Contract Database
Pennsylvania’s new Open Records Law also created an
online contract database
. State contracts valued at $5,000 or more are included in this database, which can be
searched
by agency, contracting party, contract amount, date, and subject matter.
PennWATCH: Online Budget Database
Act 18 of 2011, which I supported, requires the creation of a complete online state budget database
known as PennWATCH
. This database, designed to make details of state spending easily and freely accessible, became available on December 20, 2012.
Live Senate Video Feeds
Senate sessions can be viewed from any computer with an Internet connection using the
Senate Session Live
feed at the
Senate’s website
. A similar feed is available for
House sessions
.
Online Bill Room: Roll Call Votes and Fiscal Notes
The
General Assembly’s website
now includes links to fiscal notes for those bills that have been considered by the Senate or House Appropriations Committee. You can also access the roll call votes for every bill considered in a
Senate committee
, in a
House committee
, on the
Senate floor
, or the
House floor
.
Website for Mobile Devices
The General Assembly now has a
website for mobile devices
such as the iPhone, iPad, Android-based devices, and the BlackBerry. Visitors can use the site to search for bills by number or keyword, to read bill text, to access information about legislative committees, to watch or listen to Senate and House sessions, and to contact members of the General Assembly.
Sunshine Law: Tougher Penalties
Act 56 of 2011
, which I supported, strengthens penalties for violating Pennsylvania’s Sunshine Law, which requires public access to open meetings and the opportunity for public comment.
Senate Rules of Ethical Conduct
On June 15, 2010, the Senate adopted a set of
Rules of Ethical Conduct
to make the division between legislative and campaign work clear, to provide annual ethics training, and to establish strong penalties for violations.
Independent Fiscal Office
Pennsylvania’s new Independent Fiscal Office, created by
Act 120 of 2010
, will improve the state budget process. The office’s responsibilities include preparing annual revenue estimates, providing an annual assessment of the state’s fiscal condition, developing performance measures for state programs, and analyzing tax and revenue proposals made by the Governor or the Office of the Budget. More information is available at the
IFO’s website
.
Other Sources of Information
In addition to those listed above, the following resources provide additional information designed to make the operation of state government more transparent and accountable.
Lobbyist Disclosure Reports
Pennsylvania’s Lobbying Disclosure Law,
Act 134 of 2006
, requires lobbyists and principals (the companies and individuals who hire lobbyists) to file quarterly reports. The Department of State maintains an
online database of lobbyists, principals and the required reports
.
Statements of Financial Interest
The Governor, members of the General Assembly, and other public officials are required to file Statements of Financial Interest with the
State Ethics Commission
. The Statements of Financial Interest are all available on the Commission’s website.

Amends Title 20 (Decedents, Estates and Fiduciaries) to codify Pennsylvania Orders for Life-Sustaining Treatment (POLST) for their use and adherence as medical orders by health care providers for patients for whom a physician has determined, within reasonable medical judgment, and confirmed in writing, that an individual has a diagnosed life-limiting and irreversible condition and the individual’s health status, diagnosis and prognosis indicate that standing medical orders concerning treatment options are appropriate. Makes POLSTs voluntary for patients or their authorized surrogate decision maker to execute. Prohibits execution of an out-of-hospital do-not-resuscitate order (OOH-DNR) on or after the date the Department of Health adopts an initial POLST form while permitting previously executed OOH-DNR orders, bracelets, and necklaces to continue to be recognized as valid. Prohibits health care insurers, heath care providers, and health care facilities from requiring an individual to consent to a POLST. Requires emergency medical services (EMS) providers to comply with the instructions of an authorized medical command physician to withhold or discontinue resuscitation, notwithstanding the absence of a do-not-resuscitate order in a POLST, while requiring EMS providers to provide other necessary medical interventions for comfort, pain relief, and other appropriate interventions unless otherwise directed by the patient or the authorized medical command physician. Makes POLSTs valid throughout the Commonwealth, including in health care facilities, a patient’s residence, other care settings and during transfers. Does not prohibit do-not-resuscitate or other orders issued for care within a health care facility from being valid and actionable within that facility. Grants civil and criminal liability to a health care provider or other person who, in good faith, complies with a POLST believed to be valid, or refuses to comply with a POLST based on a good-faith belief that the POLST is invalid, compliance would be unethical or compliance would have no medical basis in addressing the patient’s medical needs. Allows for a patient or surrogate decision maker acting within decision-making authority to revoke consent to all or part of a POLST at any time and in any manner that communicates intent to revoke. Directs DOH to adopt, update and make a POLST form and education materials publicly available. Creates the POLST Advisory Committee to advise the Department on POLST-related matters.

E-news Updates - June 18, 2026 - Senator Hutchinson
View this email in a browser
In this Update:
National Guard Day at the Capitol
Senate Votes to Protect Your Right to Know About Government Actions
Making it Easier for Fire Companies, EMS Agencies to Access Funding
Flying the POW/MIA Flag at Public Schools
Quarantine Order Issued to Protect PA Farms from Screwworm
Happy Father’s Day
National Guard Day at the Capitol
I recently had the opportunity to attend an event at the Pennsylvania State Capitol in Harrisburg, where the Pennsylvania Department of Military and Veterans Affairs showcased its dual mission of supporting both the
Pennsylvania National Guard
and our veterans.
I explored interactive displays highlighting the partnerships that strengthen service to our nation, commonwealth, veterans, and communities. A memorable moment was when 18 new Army and Air National Guard members took the oath of enlistment during a ceremony led by Maj. Gen. Michael Wegscheider and Maj. Gen. Terrence Koudelka.
Senate Votes to Protect Your Right to Know About Government Actions
The Senate approved legislation to strengthen government transparency and protect the public’s right to know.
Senate Bill 1150
would clarify Pennsylvania’s Sunshine Act to ensure public agencies provide meaningful notice before acting on important matters. The bill reinforces the 24-hour agenda posting requirement and ensures exceptions for emergencies and small-scale matters remain limited.
The legislation follows a state Supreme Court ruling allowing agencies to add agenda items and take official action on them with a simple majority vote, even when those items were not included on a publicly posted agenda. The bill was sent to the House of Representatives for consideration.
Read more about legislation to strengthen the Sunshine Act here
.
Making it Easier for Fire Companies, EMS Agencies to Access Funding
Legislation to make it easier for fire and EMS agencies to access state funding through the Fire and EMS Grant program was approved by the Senate.
Senate Bill 1261
streamlines the application process, including eliminating outdated wording and incentives, using the state’s Single Application for Assistance instead of having a separate, redundant system, and asking fire companies to provide additional contact information to ensure lines of communication are open.
The bill also increases the amount fire and EMS agencies can borrow through the State Fire Commissioner’s low-interest loan program, freeing up more funding opportunities for first responder agencies. Senate Bill 1261 now advances to the House of Representatives.
Read more about these proposed improvements here
.
Flying the POW/MIA Flag at Public Schools
The Senate voted to require the POW/MIA flag be displayed at any public school in the commonwealth that already displays the American flag, provided the school can reasonably accommodate it.
By meeting the requirement of
Senate Bill 835
schools can help ensure the sacrifices of prisoners of war and those missing in action are never forgotten and demonstrate their commitment to supporting military families and educating students about the importance of service.
The bill was sent to the House of Representatives for consideration.
Read more about Senate Bill 835 here
.
Quarantine Order Issued to Protect PA Farms from Screwworm
Heightened risk of New World Screwworm (NWS) following confirmed cases in Texas and New Mexico has prompted the state Department of Agriculture to issue a quarantine order limiting the movements of livestock and pets.
There are currently no cases in Pennsylvania, but NWS is a devastating pest. Its fly larvae can infest livestock, pets, wildlife, occasionally birds, and in rare cases, people.
The quarantine order establishes movement restrictions and enhanced animal health requirements for susceptible domestic animals entering Pennsylvania from affected areas. The order includes provisions for veterinary inspection, animal health certification and preventative measures designed to reduce the risk of NWS entering the commonwealth through animal movements.
Read the NWS quarantine order here
.
Find more information about the NWS outbreak here
.
Happy Father’s Day
On Sunday, we celebrate fathers and fatherhood, and honor the dads who influenced us throughout our lives. Happy Father’s Day to all the fathers and father figures who contribute so much to our families and communities.

Working to Finalize the State Budget
Happy Independence Day!
Working to Finalize the State Budget
Good progress is being made as we work on finalizing the state budget for fiscal year 2026-27. This week, we received needed clarity on a number of issues which were delaying the budget’s completion. We’re now well on our way to reaching a full budget agreement in the coming days.
In a divided government, all parties must work together to find common ground, and I’m confident that agreement can be reached and a responsible new state budget enacted soon. My focus remains on controlling the growth of state spending and implementing pro-growth policies to protect taxpayers.
Happy Independence Day!
As we celebrate Independence Day, we honor the courage, vision, and enduring spirit of the men and women who forged the United States of America. This year’s celebration carries even greater significance as we look ahead to America250, the commemoration of our nation’s 250th anniversary. It is an opportunity to reflect on the ideals of liberty and democracy that have inspired generations and recognize the responsibility we all share to preserve those principles for the future.
Pennsylvania holds a special place in our nation’s story. From the desk of Independence Hall in Philadelphia, where the Declaration of Independence was adopted in 1776 and the U.S. Constitution was later drafted, to the countless patriots who helped shape the course of American history over the past 250 years, the Commonwealth remains at the heart of our nation’s founding – the Keystone State.
As we celebrate this Independence Day and prepare for America250, let us take pride in our shared heritage, honor those who came before us, and recommit ourselves to building an even stronger America for generations to come.

Betts Industries Celebrates 125 Years of Manufacturing
I was pleased to join Representative Rapp at an open house celebrating the 125th anniversary of Betts Industries, a longtime Warren-based, family-owned manufacturer and an important part of our region’s history and economy.
Founded in 1901, Betts has grown into an industry-leading manufacturer of critical components and lighting systems for the tank truck industry, while maintaining deep roots in Warren and a strong commitment to its employees and community.
Representative Rapp and I were honored to present President and CEO Charles Betts and Executive Vice President Ryan Betts with citations from the Pennsylvania House and Senate recognizing this remarkable milestone and 125 years of innovation, manufacturing and service.
Senate Acts to Strengthen Property Rights
Property rights are enshrined in both the U.S. and the Pennsylvania constitutions, and the Senate approved legislation to strengthen protections against warrantless entry onto private property by Pennsylvania Game Commission personnel.
Senate Bill 1431
would require Game Commission personnel to obtain a valid warrant before entering private property, including posted land, unless a judicially recognized exception to the warrant requirement applies.
Current law gives Game Commission personnel broad authority to enter land outside buildings, whether posted or otherwise. Senate Bill 1431 would place clear limits on that authority while preserving recognized exceptions to the warrant requirement.
Read more about the effort to strengthen property rights
.
Civil Air Patrol Cadets Deliver Legislative Briefing
It was a pleasure to attend a briefing hosted this week by the Senate Veterans Affairs & Emergency Preparedness Committee highlighting the important work of the Civil Air Patrol–Pennsylvania Wing and its service across the Commonwealth.
I especially enjoyed hearing from Civil Air Patrol cadets about how the program has helped them grow as individuals, prepare for future careers and develop leadership skills, all while giving them opportunities to serve their communities.
I was also honored to be sworn in as a member of the Civil Air Patrol–Pennsylvania Wing Legislative Squadron along with Representative Kathy Rapp and other members of the House and Senate.  I look forward to working with them to continue supporting CAP’s service to Pennsylvania.
School Bus Driver Safety Bill Approved by Senate
Approximately 1.5 million children are transported on school buses every day in Pennsylvania, and the Senate approved legislation aimed at keeping reckless bus drivers from getting behind the wheel.
Senate Bill 1262
would increase penalties for school bus drivers who transport children while under the influence of alcohol, a controlled substance or a dangerous combination of both.
Read more about this school bus safety measure
.
The latest Senate action follows passage last year of

, which would increase the required stopping distance for drivers approaching from the opposite direction when a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing. Both bills await passage in the House of Representatives.

Protecting Children and Families from AI Deception
It’s critical for state laws to keep up with fast-evolving Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology, especially as it relates to protecting our children online. I’m proud of our work to address the alarming rise in AI-generated sexual images of children, as well as non-consenting adults, through
Act 125 of 2024
which gives prosecutors the ability to go after criminals who create “deepfake” AI images of minors and child sexual abuse materials.
Previously, Pennsylvania law made it illegal to share intimate images without consent, and Act 125 took it a step further to combat the use of AI technology for this purpose and prohibits AI from being utilized to generate child sexual abuse material. As technology continues to advance, we must be vigilant in making sure proper safeguards are put in place.
New Law Cracks Down on Robocalls, Scam Texts and Caller ID Spoofing
Legislation we unanimously passed enacting stronger protections from deceptive telemarketing practices will take effect next month.
Under
Act 47 of 2026
, Pennsylvania’s telemarketing law will now cover modern forms of solicitation, including text messages, voicemails, ringless voicemails and robocalls. It also establishes stronger rules for when and how telemarketers can contact Pennsylvanians, including:
Prohibiting telemarketing calls before 9 a.m. and after 7 p.m. and on Sundays.
Requiring prior express written consent for most robocalls and telemarketing text messages.
Prohibiting telemarketers from falsely identifying themselves or using deceptive caller ID information, including spoofed numbers.
Requiring telemarketers to stop a solicitation when a consumer asks them to do so.
The legislation also prohibits the use of AI-generated messages to deceive consumers. The new law takes effect Oct. 19.
Phishing Scam Targets “MyChart” Patient Portal Users
If you use MyChart — a popular online patient portal used by many hospitals and healthcare providers — please be aware of a phishing scam targeting patients.
State Attorney General Dave Sunday reports scammers are impersonating MyChart by sending emails or text messages that offer patients a chance to claim a reward in the form of a “MyChart Medicare Kit.” No such program or reward exists.
These emails and text messages are attempts to trick recipients into clicking on malicious links, and obtain passwords and personal information from patients, which allows hackers to gain access to the patients’ MyChart portals.
Read about how to avoid this and other phishing scams here
.
Fire and EMS Companies Can Apply Now for State Assistance
Attention local fire companies, emergency medical services and volunteer rescue squads: Applications are being accepted for the latest round of the state Fire Company and Emergency Medical Services Grant program.
The funds can be used to help pay for facility construction/renovation, equipment, training, debt reduction and more. The application period closes Oct. 22.
Providing communities with fire, medical and rescue services comes with a considerable price tag, especially for volunteer organizations. The General Assembly funds these grants to ensure these life-saving services are available.
Find more information and applications here
.
Remembering 9/11 25 Years Later
On Sept. 11, 2001, terrorists highjacked four airliners on America’s east coast and turned them into deadly missiles, ultimately taking the lives of nearly 3,000 citizens in the name of Islamic fundamentalism.
Filled with passengers, two of the planes were flown into the World Trade Center towers in New York City and another into the Pentagon in Washington, D.C.  The fourth, perhaps destined to strike the White House or U.S. Capitol, was brought down in Somerset County by brave passengers who fought back.
Twenty-five years later, we recall the shock and anger over the attack, the grief over lives taken and the resolve to prevent another act of that scale. I hope we also remember the nation coming together in response, and the power of a unified people facing adversity. As the number of people who experienced this event declines, it becomes more important to dedicate ourselves to never letting that day slip from our nation’s memory.

Senate Stands with Attorney General, District Attorneys, State Troopers and Police
Second-degree murder is a horrific crime – these are homicides committed while the defendant was also committing another violent felony such as rape, arson, robbery, burglary or kidnapping. Those who commit such an act deserve a punishment that matches.
In March, the Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled that our current sentencing structure for second-degree murder (life without parole in every case) is unconstitutional. The justices gave the General Assembly 120 days to enact legislation correcting the situation.
The Senate
successfully passed strong bipartisan legislation to address this issue
– twice. The Senate’s legislation is supported by Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday, Pennsylvania District Attorneys, the Pennsylvania State Troopers Association, the Pennsylvania State Lodge Fraternal Order of Police, and the Pennsylvania Chiefs of Police Association.
Unfortunately, the leadership in the House of Representatives refused to allow a vote on this bipartisan legislation, instead passing a weak bill on a near party-line vote. That bill has several serious problems, including the fact that it could allow more than half of all inmates, including those on death row, to qualify for release from prison under an overbroad, ill-defined “medical release” program that is riddled with loopholes. It makes no sense.
I will continue fighting for a strong, common-sense response to the Supreme Court’s decision because the safety of our communities is at stake.
Local Eagle Scout Recognized
It was a true honor to celebrate Kale Loyal Meyers, son of Gary and Traci Jo Meyers, on his achievement of the distinguished rank of Eagle Scout. As a member of Troop 39 in Butler County, Kale demonstrated his commitment to service through his Eagle Scout project by refinishing the outdoor furniture at Magnolia Place in Saxonburg for the community to enjoy.
Kale’s Court of Honor was held at Glade Run Park, where I was delighted to present him with a Pennsylvania House of Representatives citation sponsored by Representative Marci Mustello, along with a Pennsylvania Senate citation.
Congratulations, Kale, on this remarkable achievement. Your dedication, leadership, and spirit of service are truly inspiring!

Legislation drafted after it was learned unauthorized commercial driver’s license (CDL) schools were operating in Pennsylvania is now law, significantly boosting penalties for these “CDL mills.”

increases the maximum civil penalty for operating an unauthorized CDL school from $2,500 to $25,000, giving the state Department of Education a stronger enforcement tool to stop illegal operations and discourage violations. The new law does not impact private employers that provide CDL training to their own employees at no cost.

The Pennsylvania Senate Republican Caucus (“we,” “our,” or “us”) is committed to safeguarding your privacy. This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, share, and protect your information. By using our website or engaging with our communications, you agree to the terms of this Privacy Policy.

Fighting for Affordable Energy
Rising energy costs have put added pressure on Pennsylvania families and businesses and must be addressed. This legislative session, I made it a priority to prevent new energy taxes and support energy development that strengthens reliability and helps bring costs down.
As part of the 2025-26 budget agreement, I worked with my colleagues to eliminate Pennsylvania’s participation in the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative (RGGI) – a multi-state pact that would have added more than a billion dollars in new electricity taxes.I also supported Senate passage of legislation eliminating the gross receipts tax on electric bills, which would save ratepayers more than $1.7 billion over the first year.
And this week the Senate Environmental Resources and Energy Committee advanced
Senate Resolution 374
, a resolution I sponsored directing a comprehensive study of Pennsylvania’s conventional oil and natural gas industry and its role in meeting growing energy demands. This important step recognizes the industry’s longstanding contributions to Northwest Pennsylvania’s economy, including supporting family-sustaining jobs and small businesses, while highlighting the need to preserve domestic energy production and ensure reliable, affordable energy for Pennsylvania families and employers.
Because lack of energy development drives up costs, the Senate passed legislation to reduce Pennsylvania’s electric generation shortfall and expand energy development.
Senate Bill 704
directs the state departments of Community and Economic Development and Environmental Protection to work together to identify suitable sites for natural gas electric generation projects. The House also failed to act on this measure.
I will continue fighting for lower energy prices, supporting policies which will cut your costs.
Corry Hatchery Celebrates 150 Years
I was pleased to join the celebration of a very special milestone for the
Corry State Fish Hatchery
– 150 years of service to Pennsylvania anglers!
Established in 1876 as the Western Hatchery, the Corry State Fish Hatchery is Pennsylvania’s longest continuously operating hatchery. Each year, it produces more than 300,000 trout and plays an important role in supporting our state’s fishing heritage and local economy.
The hatchery continues to thrive thanks to its dedicated Fish & Boat Commission staff, who help keep this longstanding tradition alive while welcoming approximately 5,000 visitors each year. It’s great to see a facility with so much history continue to make such a positive impact on our region.
I was proud to present a Senate citation, alongside Representative Jake Banta, who presented a House citation, recognizing this impressive anniversary and the many people who have contributed to the hatchery’s success over the years. Congratulations to everyone involved, and here’s to another 150 years!

A measure to provide lifetime no-contact orders for victims of certain serious or violent offenses was approved by the Senate.
Under current law, victims must go to court to renew no-contact protections each time they expire. Without renewal, an offender may once again attempt to contact the victim, even though the conviction, and the harm that made the protection necessary, has not changed. Unwanted contact can retraumatize victims, especially survivors of rape and other sexually violent offenses, including offenses involving the abuse or exploitation of children.
Senate Bill 1484

PSP Troop E Headquarters Dedication
On October 14, I had the pleasure of attending the dedication ceremony for the Pennsylvania State Police Troop E Headquarters. Troop E proudly serves Erie, Crawford, Venango, and Warren counties, playing an important role in keeping our communities safe.
It was a wonderful opportunity to recognize the men and women of the Pennsylvania State Police and thank them for all they do. I also want to express my sincere appreciation to our local police departments and law enforcement officers, who work hand in hand with the State Police to serve and protect our communities.
We are blessed to have so many devoted, selfless individuals who put on a uniform each day, often making personal sacrifices to keep our families and neighbors safe. Thank you to all who serve!
PA House Democrats Must Act to Protect Pennsylvania Communities
In March, the Pennsylvania Supreme Court ruled the state’s mandatory life-without-parole sentence for second-degree murder is unconstitutional. The court gave the General Assembly until July 24 to enact a new rule. The Senate passed legislation to protect our communities and fix the problem – twice.
Instead of acting on our bipartisan
Senate Bill 1400
, the House of Representatives advanced a proposal tied to expanding medical parole, creating additional opportunities – without proper guardrails – for convicted felons to be released before completing their sentences.
Senate Bill 1400 is supported by Attorney General Dave Sunday, PA State Lodge FOP, PA State Troopers Association and district attorneys across the commonwealth. It has languished in the House Judiciary Committee since June. Second‑degree murder is an extremely serious crime, and the House needs to act so these criminals remain behind bars.
New Law Means PA Schools Will Be Cellphone-Free
Pennsylvania teachers will no longer have to compete with smartphones for their students’ attention – and kids will be able to get through the school day without the constant pressure of social media and notifications – with bipartisan passage of a new law requiring schools to adopt policies prohibiting student cellphone use during the school day.
Act 117 of 2026
includes limited exceptions, such as students with individualized education plans and special occasions such as field days. It establishes a clear statewide standard, while allowing school districts, which have direct contact with parents, to decide what works best for their communities.
The law will take effect with the 2027-28 school year. Pennsylvania joins 40 states in restricting these devices – 19 of which have school-day bans.
Read more about the effect of cellphones in schools
.
Ensuring Sexual Assault Survivors Get Justice
Obtaining justice for sexual assault survivors requires timely processing of rape kit evidence, and I joined colleagues in making it a priority to improve and standardize rape kit testing.
Previously, state law allowed local law enforcement agencies to determine whether a sexual assault evidence kit should undergo DNA testing or other forensic analysis, creating the potential for inconsistent practices across the commonwealth. We passed a new law eliminating such discretion.

In addition, a law we passed in 2024 established a
rape kit evidence tracking system
, allowing survivors to track the status of their rape kits throughout the testing process. After operating as a pilot program in three counties, it will launch statewide in December.
To better care for victims, we included a $12 million increase for
rape crisis centers
in the current state budget. Prosecuting perpetrators of these heinous crimes should be pursued vigorously, and we’ve made significant changes to ensure just that.
